hook: Thomas Kipf studied physics at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in Germany, completing a bachelor's degree in 2014 and a master's with honors in 2016. He then began a PhD in computer science at the University of Amsterdam under Max Welling and Ivan Titov. In September 2016 he and Welling published Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks, which adapted convolutional neural networks to work directly on graph-structured data such as citation networks and social graphs. The paper became one of the most cited works in graph machine learning and helped launch the field of graph neural networks. He completed his PhD cum laude in 2020 and joined Google Brain in Amsterdam as a research scientist that same year. He has since worked on relational reasoning, world models, and object-centric learning, and holds the title of Senior Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind.
name: Thomas Kipf

timeline.event: Began a BSc in physics at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.
Completed an MSc in physics with honors and began a PhD in computer science at the University of Amsterdam.
Published "Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks" with Max Welling.
timeline.impact: Gave researchers a practical, widely adopted architecture for learning from graph-structured data.

timeline.event: Co-authored "Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks," winning the Best Student Research Paper Award at ESWC.
timeline.impact: Extended graph convolutional methods to knowledge graphs with multiple relation types.

timeline.event: Completed his PhD cum laude and joined Google Brain in Amsterdam as a Research Scientist.
timeline.impact: Moved his graph and relational learning research into industry research.

timeline.event: Co-authored "Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention," a NeurIPS Spotlight paper.
timeline.impact: Advanced unsupervised methods for learning object representations from visual scenes.
Recognized as one of the top PhD theses in machine learning in Europe.

timeline.event: Promoted to Senior Research Scientist at Google Research.

quick_facts: BSc and MSc in physics from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Germany
PhD in computer science from the University of Amsterdam, advised by Max Welling and Ivan Titov
Published Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks in 2016
Joined Google Brain, later Google DeepMind, in Amsterdam in 2020
Received the ELLIS PhD Award in 2021

achievements.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks (2016)
achievements.impact: Introduced a simplified, scalable way to apply convolutional operations to graph-structured data, becoming one of the foundational papers of graph neural network research.

achievements.title: Variational Graph Auto-Encoders (2016)
achievements.impact: Extended variational autoencoders to graphs, enabling unsupervised learning of graph representations.

achievements.title: Neural Relational Inference for Interacting Systems (2018)
achievements.impact: Proposed a model for inferring interactions between objects in dynamical systems directly from observed trajectories.

achievements.title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention (2020)
achievements.impact: Introduced a mechanism for decomposing visual scenes into object-like representations without supervision, earning a NeurIPS 2020 Spotlight.

achievements.title: ELLIS PhD Award (2021)
achievements.impact: Recognized his PhD research on graph-structured representation learning as among the best in Europe that year.
